newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold despite mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held relatively steady Thursday in quiet trade, underpinned by prospects for warmer East Coast weather later this week despite temperatures now that were slowing demand.

"The market felt pretty stable today. Summer is not over yet, so I don't see prices cratering anytime soon," said one cash trader, noting warmer eastern weather forecasts later this week and decent Florida demand helped support the market.
While East Coast temperatures are expected to warm to above normal later this week and early next, more seasonal weather is forecast for midweek.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped a quarter to about $16.75 a barrel on sluggish utility interest this week. Traders said August one percent paper was steady to up slightly at $16.40, helped by modest gains in crude. September paper was still quoted on either side of $16.25.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour eased slightly to about $17.75.
High sulphurs in New York held steady, with 2.2 percent still pegged at $15.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices also were stable, with one percent still in the high-$15s and three percent at $14.50-75.
Traders said 45,000 barrels of fairly prompt HSFO (8.5 gravity) sold at $14.45 (FOB Mississippi River). Another prompt 45,000-barrel deal (10.5 gravity) was reported at $14.65 (FOB Beaumont, Texas).

New York city gate swing gas prices again gained a few cents Thursday to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed four cents to $2.24/mmBtu, or $14.11 a barrel.
